$comment: Regulatory and threat-timeline policy. Every date here is externally sourced; nothing is invented. Operators override criticality tiers and migration effort for their own estate.

quantum_timeline.source: Global Risk Institute, Quantum Threat Timeline Report 2025 -- expert survey range
quantum_timeline.note: Z is contested. Q-DARPAN evaluates Mosca's inequality against all three scenarios and reports which of them trip, rather than asserting a single date.

regulatory_milestones.label: DST NQM: vendor CBOMs expected from FY 2027-28
regulatory_milestones.source: DST National Quantum Mission, Quantum Safe Ecosystem Task Force report, 4 Feb 2026

regulatory_milestones.label: NIST IR 8547 (ipd): 112-bit RSA/ECC deprecated after 2030
regulatory_milestones.source: NIST IR 8547 Initial Public Draft, 12 Nov 2024

regulatory_milestones.label: NIST IR 8547 (ipd): quantum-vulnerable algorithms disallowed after 2035
regulatory_milestones.source: NIST IR 8547 Initial Public Draft, 12 Nov 2024

criticality_tiers.$comment: Y in Mosca's inequality: how many years the protected data must stay confidential.

critical.label: National security, health records, long-lived PKI roots

migration_effort_years.$comment: X in Mosca's inequality: how long this class of asset takes to migrate. Defaults are conservative; override per target in an operator policy file.

risk_tiers.$comment: How Mosca scenarios and classical status combine into a reported tier.
risk_tiers.critical: Classically broken or disallowed, or Mosca trips under all three scenarios
risk_tiers.high: Quantum-broken and Mosca trips under the median scenario
risk_tiers.medium: Quantum-broken and Mosca trips only under the pessimistic scenario
risk_tiers.low: Quantum-weakened but Mosca does not trip
